g.title: public.organizations
g.text: Tenant root. Single row today; every domain table hangs off organization_id for future multi-tenancy.

g.title: public.locations
g.text: IANA timezone driving availability math and notification formatting. Change with care: weekly hours are interpreted in this zone.
Sales tax in basis points (800 = 8%). Applied to taxable transaction items (retail); services are non-taxable in GA.

g.title: public.staff
g.text: Employees. Linked 1:1 to auth.users via user_id. Deactivated (active=false), never deleted. Self-editable personal fields are guarded by trg_guard_staff_self_update.
Whether this person appears as a provider in scheduling (columns, qualification pickers, slot search).

g.title: public.staff_locations:location_id->public.locations:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (location_id) REFERENCES locations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.staff_locations:staff_id->public.staff:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.roles
g.text: Role definitions. system=true rows (super_admin, admin, front_desk, provider) cannot be deleted.

g.title: public.permissions
g.text: Permission catalog: domain.action(.own|.any) keys. Seeded in migration 1; code references keys as strings.

g.title: public.role_permissions
g.text: The permission matrix as data. Changing a row changes app behavior everywhere with zero deploys.

g.title: public.role_permissions:role_id->public.roles:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (role_id) REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.role_permissions:permission_key->public.permissions:key
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (permission_key) REFERENCES permissions(key) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.staff_roles
g.text: Role assignments. Audit-logged by trigger; last-super-admin removal blocked by trigger.

g.title: public.staff_roles:staff_id->public.staff:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.staff_roles:role_id->public.roles:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (role_id) REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.audit_log
g.text: Append-only. Inserts via service role / security-definer functions only. Includes health_note.viewed (app-layer, since SELECTs cannot fire triggers), appointment.booked, staff lifecycle events.

g.title: public.staff_invites
g.text: Tokenized invites (7-day expiry). Accepted atomically by accept_staff_invite() — service-role only. Partial unique index prevents duplicate pending invites per email.

g.title: public.services
g.text: The treatment catalog. duration_minutes is client-facing; buffers extend the blocked window. Prices in cents. requires_intake gates booking once intake forms exist. Deactivated, never deleted.
Cleanup/reset time appended to the blocked window; invisible to the client-facing times.

g.title: public.resource_types
g.text: Room categories services require (Massage Room, Facial Room, ...).

g.title: public.resources
g.text: Concrete rooms per location. Inactive rooms leave bookable inventory immediately.

g.title: public.service_resource_requirements
g.text: Service -> room TYPE requirement; a concrete free room of the type is assigned at booking.

g.title: public.service_resource_requirements:service_id->public.services:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (service_id) REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.service_resource_requirements:resource_type_id->public.resource_types:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (resource_type_id) REFERENCES resource_types(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.service_staff
g.text: Qualification: who may perform what, with optional per-staff duration/price overrides that the slot and booking routes apply.

g.title: public.service_staff:staff_id->public.staff:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.service_staff:service_id->public.services:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (service_id) REFERENCES services(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.clients
g.text: Spa clients (no auth accounts). no_show_count is maintained by trigger from appointment status changes. flags is an extensible jsonb for operational booleans (requires_card_on_file).
Operational booleans, extendable without migrations. Known keys: requires_card_on_file
Stripe Customer id (cus_...). Created lazily by the setup-intent route on first card save. Single platform Stripe account; a future Connect retrofit would add an account dimension here.

g.title: public.client_notes
g.text: Tiered notes: preference | internal | health. HEALTH notes are RLS-gated to clients.notes.health.view and must be read through the audited server route (reads cannot fire triggers, so auditing lives at the app layer). Append-only.

g.title: public.client_notes:client_id->public.clients:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.availability_rules
g.text: Recurring weekly hours in LOCATION-LOCAL time (survives DST). Overlaps per staff/day are impossible: no_overlapping_hours exclusion constraint (timerange custom type).

g.title: public.availability_rules:staff_id->public.staff:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.availability_exceptions
g.text: Time off / sick / breaks (remove availability) and extra shifts (add it). requested -> approved/denied workflow; decisions notify the subject and new requests notify approvers via triggers.

g.title: public.availability_exceptions:staff_id->public.staff:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.appointments
g.text: Never deleted — status lifecycle only (booked→confirmed→checked_in→in_progress→completed | cancelled | no_show). Double-booking of staff or rooms is impossible: gist exclusion constraints on the blocked window, which ignore cancelled/no_show rows so slots free themselves.
Start of the FULL blocked window including buffer_before — what all conflict checks use.

g.title: public.appointment_services
g.text: Line items with name/price/duration SNAPSHOTS taken at booking: catalog edits never rewrite booked history.

g.title: public.appointment_services:appointment_id->public.appointments:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (appointment_id) REFERENCES appointments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.notifications
g.text: In-app notifications. Created ONLY by triggers/service role (no authenticated insert policy). RLS scopes reads and mark-read to the recipient — including over Realtime, which is published for this table.

g.title: public.notifications:staff_id->public.staff:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.products
g.text: Retail catalog (lotions, candles, ...). Stock decremented by trigger on sale. cost_cents enables margin reporting. Deactivated, never deleted.

g.title: public.gift_cards
g.text: Balance maintained by triggers: created/loaded by a gift_card SALE item, decremented by a gift_card PAYMENT. Balance can never go negative (trigger).

g.title: public.transactions
g.text: The immutable money ledger: one row per checkout. NEVER updated or deleted (no policies exist). Refunds are new rows with negative amounts referencing the original via refunds_transaction_id. All financial reporting reads from here.

g.title: public.transaction_items
g.text: Line items with name/price SNAPSHOTS (catalog edits never rewrite sold history). kind=service carries appointment + staff attribution; kind=tip carries staff attribution for payroll reads; kind=discount is negative; kind=gift_card is a liability sale, excluded from revenue reporting.

g.title: public.transaction_items:transaction_id->public.transactions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (transaction_id) REFERENCES transactions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.payments
g.text: How each transaction settled. Multiple rows = split tender ("$80 gift card + rest on card"). card_external = charged on the spa's existing physical terminal and recorded here; in-app charging arrives with Stripe (4b).
Set on method=stripe_card rows (pi_...). The refund route calls stripe.refunds.create against this. The sync charge flow guarantees it: ledger rows are written only after the PaymentIntent succeeds.

g.title: public.payments:transaction_id->public.transactions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (transaction_id) REFERENCES transactions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.conversations
g.text: DMs and ad-hoc group chats. updated_at is bumped by every message (list sort key). Append-only messaging: no edit/delete in v1.

g.title: public.conversation_participants
g.text: Membership + read state. last_read_at is the unread mechanism: unread = messages newer than it. Rows are created only by the conversation functions (security definer).

g.title: public.conversation_participants:staff_id->public.staff:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES staff(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.conversation_participants:conversation_id->public.conversations:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (conversation_id) REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.messages
g.text: Append-only (no update/delete policies). Org-scoped through the parent conversation (transaction_items precedent). Published to realtime; RLS limits delivery to participants.

g.title: public.messages:conversation_id->public.conversations:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (conversation_id) REFERENCES conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.card_consents
g.text: Consent records for storing a card on file (cancellation-fee enabler). Append-only: no update/delete policies. method=front_desk_attested is v1; client_signed arrives with intake forms. policy_text is a snapshot of the exact language shown at capture.

g.title: public.client_payment_methods
g.text: Display-fields-only mirror of Stripe PaymentMethods (pm_...). consent_id is NOT NULL: no card exists without a consent record. Detached/expired cards are deactivated (active=false), never deleted — historical payments may reference them.

g.title: public.stripe_events
g.text: Processed Stripe webhook event ids for idempotency. Insert-on-arrival; unique violation = duplicate delivery, skip. Service-role only (no policies).

g.title: public.ask_queries
g.text: Append-only record of every Ask The Reserve question: the text asked, the SQL that ran, what came back, and what it cost. No update/delete policies — a query log that can be edited is not a query log. Written by the /api/ask route; readable with ask.query. Rows with a non-null error are failed generations, which is the signal for prompt work. Rows with a null model are the preset path: answered with human-written SQL, no tokens spent.
The exact statement handed to ask_execute_sql, model-written or preset. Shown to the admin behind the "show the query" affordance and kept here for after-the-fact review.
Which model answered, e.g. claude-opus-5. Null on the preset path — no model was called, which is the point of presets.
Uncached input tokens billed at full rate. The cached schema prompt lands in cache_read_tokens instead, so this stays small on a warm cache.

Tokens served from the prompt cache (~0.1x input price). The system prompt is identical on every ask, so a healthy value here is the sign caching is working; a persistent zero means something is invalidating the prefix.

What this ask cost, in MILLIONTHS of a dollar (22500 = $0.0225). Cents would round a two-cent ask to nothing. Priced at the rate in force when it ran and never recomputed — a rate change must not rewrite history.

Groups the asks of one dock session, bounded by the "New thread" control. Null on rows written before threading existed, and on any ask made outside a thread. A refined question ("and who used it?") is only interpretable alongside the rows sharing its thread_id — note that generated_sql on each row stays self-contained, so an ANSWER is always auditable on its own; it is the question TEXT that needs its predecessors.

The question with its references resolved against the thread — "and who used it?" recorded as "which clients redeemed gift cards in the last 2 months?". Equal to question on a first turn, where there is nothing to resolve. Null on the preset path (no model ran) and on rows written before this column existed. Read THIS when auditing an answer or mining the log; `question` keeps what was literally typed, which is what the admin will recognise.

g.title: public.form_definitions
g.text: A form's IDENTITY (org + key), separate from its answerable shape, which lives in versioned form_versions rows. One row per form the business asks people to fill: prospect_intake, service_waiver. Deactivated, never deleted — a definition with responses against it must stay resolvable forever.
Stable machine name the code refers to (prospect_intake, service_waiver). Never renamed: responses reach their definition through it, and a rename would silently re-point them.

g.title: public.form_versions
g.text: One immutable published shape of a form. APPEND-ONLY BY DESIGN: no update or delete policy exists, so Postgres denies both, and the revoke below states that intent out loud. Editing a form means inserting a new version. That immutability is what lets a response REFERENCE the shape it answered instead of copying it — change a version in place and every response that points at it silently changes meaning.

Ordered array of field descriptors: [{"key","label","type","required","sensitive"}]. sensitive=true routes an answer to form_response_health instead of form_responses.answers — it is the switch that decides whether an answer needs clients.notes.health.view to read. Postgres cannot validate this shape; the server route that accepts submissions is the only enforcement, which is why it is the tested one.
The waiver/consent copy shown with THIS version. Copied onto each response at submit (form_responses.consent_text) — the reference here is provenance; the copy there is the legal record.

g.title: public.form_versions:form_definition_id->public.form_definitions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (form_definition_id) REFERENCES form_definitions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.form_responses
g.text: One filled-in form. answers holds ONLY the non-sensitive answers; anything the version marks sensitive is in form_response_health, behind clients.notes.health.view. No authenticated INSERT policy exists on purpose: a submission must be validated against its version's field list, Postgres cannot check jsonb shape, so writes go through a server route under the service role and the validator is the enforcement.

The subject, when an existing client fills a waiver. Nullable because phase 2 adds prospect_intake_id for people who have no client record yet, and widens form_responses_subject to "exactly one subject". Until then the check requires a client.

Physical snapshot of the consent copy this person actually agreed to, readable without joining the version. Same discipline as the card-consent policy_text snapshot: the legal record must not depend on a lookup years later.

g.title: public.form_responses:client_id->public.clients:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.form_responses:form_version_id->public.form_versions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (form_version_id) REFERENCES form_versions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.form_response_health
g.text: Answers to fields the form version marks sensitive — health history and the like. A SEPARATE TABLE rather than a column on form_responses because RLS is row-level and cannot hide a column: as rows, the database itself refuses them to anyone without clients.notes.health.view, so a route that forgets to filter returns nothing rather than leaking PHI. Same tier as client_notes.kind='health', which is where these are promoted on enrollment.
The question as it was asked, snapshotted. An answer of "yes" is meaningless without the question, and the version's field list can be superseded by a later publish.

g.title: public.form_response_health:form_response_id->public.form_responses:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (form_response_id) REFERENCES form_responses(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
